C1.worst_defect: The hero itself is clear, but the home page below it turns into docs a first-timer cannot parse: the comparison table's refund cell reads "The refund stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls", and "Before you start" lists "Node ^20.19 || >=22.12" and "RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)" on the marketing page.
C1.where: home/desktop/02 ('Live demo or your own store' refund row, 'Before you start'); home/phone/04

C2.worst_defect: The home page's demo row says the demo "sends anonymous usage events to ph.wcpos.com". A second brand's domain shows up with no word on who wcpos is or how it relates to VendurePOS, so a newcomer wonders whose product this really is.
C2.where: home/desktop/02 'Sales reach Vendure, once each, even offline' row; home/phone/04

C3.worst_defect: Step 6 makes you change the store-wide orderTaxCalculationStrategy and warns "These settings are store-wide and also affect the web shop". It never says what changes for the existing web shop's totals, so a developer with a live store has to guess whether turning on the POS will move their online prices.
C3.where: quick-start/desktop/03 '6. Choose tax rounding for your pricing mode'

C4.worst_defect: The changelog's "In short" summaries help, but its bullets are internal shorthand nobody outside the project can read: "order.create v5 custom lines ... (ADR 0005)", "TallyPosV51790900000000", "lineTax: { none: true, classes: true }". The ADR and issue links point into the repo and are never explained on the site.

C5.worst_defect: In 'What it does today', the first two features sit in bordered cards with buttons and the other eight are plain unboxed text in a two-column grid. The section looks half-converted rather than deliberately ranked.

C6.worst_defect: Headings with inline code wrap to three lines and crowd the top of each step on a phone, e.g. "2. Add TallyPosPlugin to your existing Vendure config" and "3. Generate and run the migration before starting the server".

C7.worst_defect: The share card's demo screenshot is cropped hard at the bottom edge, through the product price badges and the half-visible "Add charge" button, so the card looks cut off rather than framed.

overall_worst.defect: After a clear hero, the home page's lower half reads as setup docs: the refund cell explains Pending refunds and "two Admin API calls", and 'Before you start' lists Node semver ranges, Postgres versions and an RXDB_PREMIUM licence token. A first-time visitor deciding in under a minute meets this jargon wall and gets no plain 'what you need' summary.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/02 and home/phone/04 ('Live demo or your own store' refund row, 'Before you start')
overall_worst.fix: Shorten the refund cell to "No, refund in the Vendure Dashboard for now (see Limitations)". Cut 'Before you start' down to three plain lines (a Vendure 3.6+ store on Postgres, the plugin, a desktop browser) linking to the Overview's requirements, and move the Node, RxDB and Admin API details there.
